html:
The Nazca lines are huge designs drawn on the desert floor of southern Peru by the Nazca people, mostly between about 500 BCE and 500 CE. They include straight lines many kilometres long, shapes, and figures of animals and plants.

The Nazca made them by removing the dark stones on the surface to show the lighter ground below. Among the figures are a hummingbird, a monkey, a spider and a killer whale, some hundreds of metres across. The dry, windless climate has kept them for two thousand years. Many are best seen from the air, which has led to fanciful theories, but they could be made with simple tools and cords.

Most scholars think they were paths for rituals, linked to water and fertility in a land where rain was scarce. The German scholar Maria Reiche studied and protected them for decades. They became a World Heritage Site in 1994. Their makers were heirs of the Paracas weavers of Peru.
sum: The Nazca lines are huge designs drawn on the desert floor of southern Peru by the Nazca people, mostly between about 500 BCE and 500 CE. They include straight lines many kilometres long, shapes, and figures of animals and plants.
